name: C++

image.dockerfile:
FROM debian:trixie-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends gcc g++ make libc6-dev && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

conventions: C++20 compiled with `-std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all`. The code under test is `solution.hpp` + `solution.cpp` in starter/, solution/ and every bugs/<name>/ (the header is identical in all). `tests/Makefile` compiles `test.cpp` with `-I../$(TARGET) ../$(TARGET)/*.cpp` into a binary under /tmp and runs it (copy the Makefile from the example). `tests/test.cpp` uses the CHECK helpers from the example: each check prints `[ok]   <name>` or `[FAIL] <name>` with expected/got, and main prints `ALL TESTS PASSED` only when there are zero failures (exit 1 otherwise). `bugs[].expect` is the failing check's name. The starter must COMPILE under -Werror and return a wrong placeholder. Favor modern C++: RAII, value semantics, std::string_view/span, algorithms over raw loops, move semantics, constexpr where natural.

levelNotes.3: Good topics: std::vector/std::unordered_map usage, string_view pitfalls (dangling), const-correctness.
levelNotes.5: Good depth topics: rule of 0/3/5, move semantics, RAII wrappers, templates with concepts, iterators for a custom container.
levelNotes.7: Good depth topics: allocator-aware containers, variant/visit state machines, exception safety guarantees, small-buffer optimization.

areas.name: RAII and ownership (unique_ptr, rule of zero)
Move semantics and the rule of five
